content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} state sales tax plus a county rate, set by where the sale takes place. A yearly governmental services tax, based on the vehicle's original price, is the largest ongoing cost.

howItWorks.text: The state rate is {stateRate}. A trade-in lowers the price the tax is figured on.
The county rate depends on the county where the sale takes place, not on where you live.
If you bought in another state and its tax was lower than Nevada's, you owe the difference. If it was higher, nothing more is due.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Nevada?
faq.text: Yes, the tax is figured on the net selling price after the trade-in.
The county where the sale takes place, not the buyer's home county.
